newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity moves higher with physicals, gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity moves higher with physicals, gas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Tuesday in line with stronger short-term physical power prices in the U.S. West and stronger natural gas prices, industry sources said.
Short-term physical electricity prices jumped on news of an unexpected outage at the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit in Arizona.
Arizona Public Service said it expects to restore output from Palo Verde 1 late Wednesday or possibly earlier following repairs to a valve leak.
Next-day peak Palo Verde (PV) power for Wednesday delivery was said to have traded in the $30.00-38.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range from $18.00-21.00 on Friday for Tuesday delivery.
Next-day peak California Oregon Border (COB) power was said to have traded at $24.50 from $18.50-19.50 per MWh.

As of 1245 EDT, June NYMEX PV power was trading up $2.85 at $28.00 following trades in a range of $27.25-28.50, while July was up $1.76 at the day's high of $31.10 after reaching a low of $29.50 per MWh.

June COB futures were up $2.33 at the day's high of $21.70 from trade as low as $20.60, while July was up $1.99 at $23.30 after hitting a new contract high of $24.00 and trading as low as $22.90 per MWh.
As of 1205 EDT, NYMEX said an estimated total of 89 COB and 203 PV contracts had traded.
"Natural gas is flying, things are picking up here," said one New York-based futures trader.
As of 1240 EDT, June Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 3.5 cents at $2.32 per million British thermal units.
June COB and PV electricity futures expire today, and sources said the vast majority of exchanges Tuesday were not expected to go to delivery.
"We're seeing lots of paper to paper trades here," the New York source said.

Separately, Bonneville Power Administration said it was offering 300 MW of firm, peak power for Wednesday deliveries at $22.00-25.00 per MWh. The federal agency has remained out of the peak power market for weeks during hydropower management at its Northwest generation facilities.

A total of about 7,000 megawatts (MW) of power generation remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance. Much of the idled generation was expected to return to service over the next several weeks, however.
The 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit was expected to begin production May 29 from a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began April 19.
Several coal-fired plants are also expected back at the end of month including the 750 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and 750 MW Four Corners unit in Arizona.
Restart of the 550 MW unit 2 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was heard postponed to June 4 from this weekend.
Forecasters expect temperatures in the Southwest to be near-normal through much of the week and rise to one to five degrees above normal by the weekend, under partially cloudy skies.
The maximum temperature in Phoenix, Ariz., Tuesday was expected to be near 92 degrees Fahrenheit.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be one to five degrees below normal through much of the week and then rise to one to five degrees above normal by the weekend. Sunny skies were expected through much of the week.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
